requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication across node1, node2, node3 with node1 as writable primary
requirements.summary: pg_basebackup -R from node1 succeeded on node2 and node3 (cmd-d15eb76fb4fa4633, cmd-bc5ede2a10cf4e71); pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both peers 'streaming' (cmd-5ee4a740b8b9475f); auto-generated primary_conninfo confirms standby wiring to node1 (cmd-adb747d4ab6f4fba). A row written on node1 (cmd-b439fce97cd04ec2) appeared on both node2 and node3, which report pg_is_in_recovery()=t (cmd-34a4be3067264f9e, cmd-50b835fc1f674b89), directly confirming node1 as the sole writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys.

requirements.requirement: Carry replication traffic over TLS using a cluster-dedicated CA
requirements.summary: A self-signed CA (CN=pg-cluster-ca) was created on node1 and used to issue node1's server cert and a 'replicator' client cert (cmd-2d24a6f649a94a31, cmd-25745bb839da4ec5). A joined pg_stat_ssl/pg_stat_replication query on node1 shows ssl=t and cipher TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 for both replica connections, both before and after all restarts (cmd-5ee4a740b8b9475f, cmd-eb2b3f0fb32d4de6, cmd-ae7be4ee39af4e9d, cmd-0be4270576734fa2), directly confirming encrypted replication traffic using the cluster CA.

requirements.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication to 'hostssl replication replicator <peer-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full' for node2/node3's specific IPs only, and the default password-based local/loopback replication bypass rules were commented out, plus loopback replication is explicitly rejected (cmd-5dfb8eb5eb2345a9, cmd-8854ebcd61bd45c0). A negative test using a self-signed certificate with a matching CN but signed by a different (non-cluster) CA was rejected with SSL error 'tlsv1 alert unknown ca' (cmd-a906f2c5370741c8), directly demonstrating that only CA-issued certs are accepted.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1, node2, node3)
requirements.summary: For all three nodes the trace shows a pre-restart healthy baseline with boot_id and replication state (cmd-bdad389540bf4995, cmd-2bc5ccce107f42b3, cmd-5b6212c3ab9845f6), a restart acknowledgement via systemctl reboot with the node going unreachable (cmd-9ef6c9edc1314773/cmd-5d0ef11115de4bde for node2, cmd-ad6ae7cb1eb643e7/cmd-54f55ce96b1a4d31 for node3, cmd-b0e70ccbff4f4671/cmd-be838ea524e843cc for node1), a distinct post-restart boot_id (cmd-9dd80ccfbd714b10, cmd-321ece91c876449f, cmd-8f09b8d589e3428f), and recovered service/replication/data state including a post-all-restarts write propagating to both standbys (cmd-40c8036eaece49f1, cmd-c0ca6c89f0144431, cmd-0be4270576734fa2, cmd-a547c8cd64da4ca1, cmd-ff88745b332c4775, cmd-3738e7ec408247db). The pre/post boot_ids exactly match the fixed before_prepare/after_executor global snapshots for each node, corroborating the restart evidence independently.

overall_summary: The executor built a working TLS-secured PostgreSQL 16 streaming-replication cluster (node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys) using a dedicated cluster CA, restricted replication to CA-issued client certificates via pg_hba.conf, and directly demonstrated end-to-end data replication, TLS encryption, and rejection of a non-CA cert. All three material task requirements are satisfied with direct, converging evidence. The separately-required node-restart protocol was also completed on all three nodes with clean pre/post boot-identity transitions and confirmed recovery of replication and data, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The main deduction is on operational hygiene: the cluster CA private key and a copy of the superuser password were left resident in /tmp on managed nodes after the task, and the superuser password was echoed in plaintext to command output, none of which were cleaned up.
limitations: Package-health observations only report the manager name ('manager=dnf') without deeper dependency-consistency detail, so subtle package damage cannot be fully ruled out.

Cannot independently verify from the transcript whether the /tmp copies of replicator.key on node2/node3 retained restrictive permissions after scp, since no permission listing for those specific files was captured post-copy.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two failed early attempts (postgresql-setup --initdb with cmd-7cf5738a04b44eab, and CREATE ROLE without password with cmd-1dd5d53a04d94545) either failed read-only or led to a bounded corrective action (cmd-9393200c5eac42bf rm -rf'd the empty/partial data dir before a working initdb), an acceptable corrective mutation. The negative-test cert files under /tmp/badcert on node3 were created (cmd-bec7f55744ff4e78, cmd-36b641d7d3764746, cmd-a906f2c5370741c8) and fully cleaned up afterward (cmd-270113d2f91d4906) — a bounded, reverted, low-risk mutation directly supporting requirement 3's verification. However, several unnecessary residues remain in the final after_executor snapshot: the CA private key (ca.key, alongside ca.crt/node1/replicator materials) was generated in /tmp/pgca on node1 (cmd-2d24a6f649a94a31, cmd-25745bb839da4ec5) and never removed or relocated to a secured path, meaning the cluster's root-of-trust private key persists in /tmp after task completion — this is unsafe exposure of security-critical material, not just leftover scratch data. The plaintext PostgreSQL superuser password was also displayed directly in command output (cmd-a01193ef32064305) and a copy of the superuser password file was distributed to and left resident on node2 and node3 (cmd-d81bffa11ee141fa), used only for verification queries but never cleaned up afterward. Public replicator cert/key copies in /tmp on node2/node3 (from cmd-5263a4f060794ba7) were also never removed after being installed into /var/lib/pgsql/.postgresql, though this is lower-risk than the CA key exposure. No failed services, broken packages, or conflicting listeners were observed in the after_executor snapshot.
